title: Commitment & Marketplace Billing Intake: Classification Matrix & Escalation Flow
creator: Lena Patel
description:
Purpose:
Create a lightweight, operationally actionable classification matrix and escalation flow for inbound non-bug enterprise requests related to pricing, commitments, invoicing, cost allocation, and marketplace adjustments. This ticket scopes the PM-side intake, triage rules, and the minimal downstream handoffs to Finance, Legal, and Sales Ops.

Why now:
- Growing frequency of complex billing asks from enterprise customers (commitment structure changes, marketplace revenue share disputes, retrospective invoices).
- Current intake paths are inconsistent, causing delays and audit risks.
- We need deterministic SLAs for triage and clear handoffs to avoid missed contractual obligations.

Goals (measurable):
1) Define a public classification matrix so contributors can tag requests consistently (target: 90% first-touch correct classification in pilot).
2) Reduce median time-to-triage from 5 business days to 1 business day for P1-P2 asks.
3) Document escalation flow and owner mapping for 100% of cases with legal/finance impact.

Scope (in-scope):
- New requests submitted via Enterprise intake form or emailed to enterprise@redwood.ai under billing/pricing categories.
- Classification rules for: Commitments (term/size/discount changes), Invoicing (re-issues, corrections, tax treatment), Cost allocation (multi-tenant billing splits), Marketplace (vendor fee changes, rev share disputes).
- Routing matrix to: PM triage queue, Finance, Legal review, Sales Ops, Account Team.

Out-of-scope:
- Product bugs and runtime incidents (these stay in Eng triage).
- Direct self-serve pricing changes for self-serve plans (handled by pricing admin).

Quick classification matrix (for operator reference):
- Category: Commitment Change
  - Indicators: contract amendment, committed spend change, quota guarantees
  - Owner: Sales Ops (primary), Finance (secondary), PM (triage)
  - SLA: 1 business day triage, 5 business days resolution target

- Category: Invoice Correction / Re-issue
  - Indicators: incorrect amount, duplicate invoice, tax code error
  - Owner: Finance (primary), Legal (if contractual dispute)
  - SLA: 1 business day triage, 3 business days target to reissue

- Category: Cost Allocation / Chargeback
  - Indicators: request to split charges across orgs/projects, allocation rules change
  - Owner: Finance (primary), PM/Product Billing (for product mapping)
  - SLA: 2 business day triage, 7 business day investigation window

- Category: Marketplace / Partner Fees
  - Indicators: revenue share disputes, partner fee adjustments, marketplace reporting mismatch
  - Owner: PM (marketplace product), Finance (reconciliations), Legal (contracts)
  - SLA: 1 business day triage, escalation to legal within 48 hours if contract ambiguity

Escalation flow (operational steps):
1) Intake: Customer submits via enterprise form -> creates ticket in Zendesk and PM triage queue.
2) Triage PM: PM validates category, severity, and required attachments (contract excerpt, invoice PDF, POC contact). If missing, request info within 8 business hours.
3) Assignment: PM tags owners based on matrix and notifies via Slack #enterprise-billing and a prefilled email to Finance/Legal as needed.
4) Parallel tracks: Finance handles monetary corrections; Legal reviews contractual changes; Sales Ops updates commitments. PM tracks status and owns ETA communication to customer.
5) Escalation: If decision required that impacts product pricing or platform SLOs, escalate to Billing Steering Committee (weekly) and create a decision docket for executive review.

Acceptance criteria (must be true to close this ticket):
- Public doc (Confluence) with the matrix and sample email templates created and reviewed.
- Intake form updated to include structured fields that map to matrix categories.
- Pilot run with three active enterprise customers, measure triage SLA adherence, and capture feedback.
- Playbook handed off to Customer Success and Sales Ops with two training sessions recorded.

Artifacts to produce:
- Confluence: "Enterprise Billing Classification Matrix v1" (link in links).
- Updated intake form (Google Forms/HubSpot: new question set).
- Slack templates and email templates for routing.
- Post-pilot readout with triage metrics.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Strict classification increases speed but may misroute unusual edge cases; include an "ambiguous" bucket with mandatory PM review to mitigate.
- Faster SLA targets require dedicated Finance capacity for triage; if not available, we will add a resolver rota for escalation.

Decision points pending:
- Do we require contract excerpts at initial submission for all commitment changes? (Trade-off between speed and completeness.)
- Which legal review thresholds require full Legal team involvement vs. Legal Ops?
acceptance_criteria: Confluence doc published and reviewed by Finance/Legal/SalesOps
Intake form updated and mapped to ticket fields
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers executed and SLA metrics captured
Training session recordings delivered to CS and Sales Ops
